name: survey-overlay-toggle
description: Player-controlled survey confidence overlay visibility (#496): the header toggle hides only the overlay mesh, leaving survey results and panel cards intact, and a new survey arriving while hidden must not silently re-show it.

steps.description: Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for tighter survey estimates -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.
Real click path: open the Survey panel, pick seismic (the method a geology-skilled surveyor can actually run), dispatch, target the tile.
Padding for the seismic survey to resolve

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Screenshot the overlay visible by default, colour-coded confidence quads over the surveyed area. `survey show` (command mode) only lists pending surveys -- read-only, unrelated to overlay visibility -- so it's paired here rather than driving the step; the Survey panel opened by the survey click above stays open across the tick/event padding steps, so this step only needs to re-frame the camera and capture, not reopen anything (clicking the toolbar toggle again would close it -- togglePanel in UIManager.ts).

Click the overlay toggle button — the overlay disappears, leaving clean terrain, while survey results stay in the panel. `state full` (command mode) is a plain read paired with the click, same convention as other pure-UI steps across this suite.
A second survey is run while the toggle is off. The Survey panel is already open (from the first survey, never closed since), so this reuses the run flow directly rather than reopening the panel.
